Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

stoppingDecision.assessment: One option integrates the quantitative and financial strands. An insurance and pensions direction lacks courses in pricing, reserving and life-contingency models. A more computational variant would replace economic and financial applications with general algorithms or machine learning, weakening its response to actuarial risk. A broader policy route would similarly dilute the quantitative-financial spine. These variants do not justify an additional option.

analysis: The principal overlap is the combination of quantitative uncertainty and financial applications. UCR covers distributions, inference and simulation, Bayesian and Markov decision models, regression, numerical methods, predictive validation, asset pricing, interest-rate exposure, bank capital and liquidity. These are substantive tools and applications for studying risk. Public Economics treats social insurance as policy, not actuarial valuation. Database Management Systems provides a supported description-only contribution in SQL, relational modelling and data preparation, rather than alignment to introductory actuarial science. Description-only Advanced Calculus, Behavioral Economics and Econometrics contribute multivariable analysis, actual decision behaviour and applied regression, respectively. Behavioral Economics moves to the final autumn. Computational & Numerical Methods and Optimization Methods in AI replace two broader business selections and add convergence, approximation and constrained optimisation. Early programming and linear algebra support later work. No workbook sequence teaches insurance pricing and reserving, life contingencies and pension liabilities. A second data-centred schedule with algorithms, deep learning and reinforcement learning would duplicate the useful methods while losing financial applications, and a policy-focused programme would lose quantitative risk. Neither offers a second substantiated response to the exact target. All positive pairings were tested against the external course descriptions or explicit programme subjects; general databases are no longer paired to the actuarial introduction.
